comparison: Perfect agreement on single-cell landscape characterization (C39-C47). Both evaluations find the cell clustering, quality control, and ferroptosis gene expression analysis to be well-supported with solid methodology.

Strong agreement on T cell subpopulation analysis (C48-C55). Both evaluations support the NMF-based identification and pseudotime analysis. Peer review explicitly highlights this as a strength with 'highly insightful' clustering and correlation with prognosis.

Agreement on transcription factor activity findings (C56-C57). OpenEval supports the TF analysis and mechanistic integration with ferroptosis. Peer review implicitly accepts these findings as part of the overall T cell characterization they praise.

Strong agreement on macrophage subpopulation characterization (C58-C65). Both evaluations support the identification of TREM2+ and FOLR2+ subtypes. Peer review specifically highlights these macrophage subtypes as a key strength linked to prognosis.

Agreement on macrophage functional characterization (C66-C68). OpenEval supports the correlation data and cell-cell communication analysis. Peer review accepts these findings as part of the macrophage subtype analysis they explicitly endorse.

Agreement on prognostic model development (C69-C72). Both evaluations support the Cox regression and LASSO methodology with reported performance metrics. Peer review affirms the model holds potential for prognosis and treatment guidance.

Divergence on external validation interpretation (C7-C9, C73). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to substantial performance drop (AUCs 0.65-0.71 vs training 0.87-0.88), suggesting potential overfitting. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, focusing on the model's overall potential without highlighting the validation performance gap.

Perfect agreement on independent prognostic value (C74-C75). Both evaluations support the multivariate Cox regression showing risk score independence. Peer review implicitly accepts these findings as part of validated methodology.

Agreement on immune infiltration analysis (C76-C78, C108). Both evaluations support the findings of specific cell type differences despite no overall immune score differences. Peer review accepts these as valid and relevant for the TNBC field.

Divergence on drug sensitivity predictions (C79-C80, C10). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing these are in silico predictions requiring experimental validation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, viewing them as valuable for guiding treatment selection without noting validation limitations.

Similar divergence on additional drug sensitivity predictions (C81-C82). OpenEval maintains UNCERTAIN rating due to lack of experimental validation. Peer review implicitly accepts these as part of the model's clinical utility.

Perfect agreement on negative immunotherapy prediction result (C83). Both evaluations support this as a valid negative finding. OpenEval notes it's clearly stated; peer review accepts the transparent reporting of this null result.
Perfect agreement on TNBC background and rationale (C1-C3, C13-C20). Both evaluations support the well-cited characterization of TNBC challenges and the research question's relevance.

Divergence on infiltration-outcome correlation claims (C4-C6). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct statistical evidence linking scRNA-seq subpopulations to clinical outcomes (connection is indirect through bulk RNA-seq model). Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, highlighting correlation with prognosis as 'highly insightful' without noting the indirect nature of this relationship.
